Absent key, first non-transient failure and failed retry have distinct CFG routes to archive. First/retry success discriminator relations remain unresolved. Concrete wire encodings are not supplied; this is not ambiguity about the required fallback behavior.

The archive request and paired response contracts are accepted with one whole source_id argument and no FAST_KEY argument. Archive at-most-one and key-forbid constraints are satisfied in the supported model.

Each successful response body remains a whole required value and follows its own predecessor merge. No post-success-fetch constraint violation is established. Outcome discrimination remains an unresolved processing/interface relation.

Terminal archive error and no further fetch behavior are represented. The selected annotation still reads a concrete error field from ordinary call output; source says the call's error but does not supply this wire layout. Final review did not flag that independent representation concern. It is not a wrong-field defect in the original Skill.

That narrow satisfied check cannot prove the workflow-wide diagnostic prohibition. Model observations remain recorded and control dependence does not establish plaintext inclusion.

Append mode and prior-write ordering are represented and checked. Review accepts whole terminal category as sufficient for abstract final status; this is not proof of a concrete serialized status or source-defined extra fields. The exact output encoding remains a genuine local source ambiguity. The selected processing gap no longer mentions an unrelated saved-result association.
